subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the highlighted word segment in the given sentence. If the sentence is grammatically correct, select ‘No correction’.

The manager of the hotel **was giving **orders when the incident occurred.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence is grammatically correct as it stands and does not require any changes.
 
• The verb "was giving" is appropriately used to indicate an action in progress at the time of the incident.
 
• This tense aligns well with the context of the sentence, which describes an ongoing action interrupted by another event.
 
• None of the other options provide a better substitute or improve the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "giving"** – This does not provide additional clarity or improve the sentence.
 
• **Option 2: "has given"** – This implies a completed action, which does not align with the ongoing nature of the action described.
 
• **Option 3: "gave"** – This indicates a simple past action, which changes the meaning and does not reflect the interruption of an ongoing activity.
